content_html_sanitized:
The second wave came in the 1970s, when the publication of the Schafer Commission and other research reports from various governments threatened prohibition.

This era began the latest research theme that continues today. This line is based on the claim that although cannabis has been used for thousands of years, we have just discovered that it does horrible things.

The great thing about this line from the prohibitionist perspective is that the research is always published in academic journals that are not easily accessed by would-be critics, not that there are many in the media. They are also couched in language that is not easily understood by the layperson. The scientists who produce this work know that NIDA funds 85% of the research on cannabis, and controls access to cannabis for any study, so they have to be careful about their questions and answers.

The good news for the scientists is that they really don't have to lie about their scientific data, so long as they give NIDA a good press release that emphasizes the most negative possible interpretation of their data. Sometimes the conclusions in their press release do not even follow from their data.
See
How NIDA Made Monkeys of the Media. 4 Primates Are News; 4 Million People Are Not. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and links

The Reagan era did not have to do much in the way propaganda about cannabis, because of the crack epidemic that they had created, and because Nancy Reagan's Just Say No campaign was so perfectly mindless. It was intended to stifle all thought, and it certainly seemed to have worked for Reagan.

This period of relative stagnation in the propaganda continued under the first Bush and William Bennett, the former drug-addicted drug czar, perhaps because Bennett was so arrogant and slovenly that he thought it unnecessary to come up with anything catchy.

The third wave of prohibitionist propaganda began with Barry McCaffrey, who was one of the most prolific liars in recent years, and recognized the threat posed by the medical marijuana initiatives. McCaffrey authorized the Institute of Medicine Report, and when it did not say what he wanted, he simply lied about it.
See
The First Anniversary of the IOM Report And The Lies and Hatred Continue, Business As Usual. Analysis By Richard Cowan

The themes that dominated this era included lying about The Netherlands.
See
Drug Czar Uses Foreign Affairs Magazine Article For Anti-Dutch Propaganda,
Elevating The Lying To Official Status. Analysis By Richard Cowan

Another feature is the potent pot line, which claims that today's marijuana is so more potent than it was back in the 60s when everyone thought that it was harmless.
See
UN Nark Prohibitionist Propaganda Organization Issues Annual Report; Uses Potent Pot Line To Justify More Marijuana Prohibition

However, he has already been surpassed by his successor, John Walters. I call this the era of hyper-lying. Goebbels on steroids.
See
The Myth That The Washington Post and John Walters Are Harmless; Drug Czar Puts Hyperlying About Cannabis At The Center of the War on Freedom.

It has some new elements. One of the cleverest features of this new line is the claim that the number marijuana addicts in treatment proves that cannabis is highly addictive. Almost two-thirds of the people in treatment for marijuana are sent by the courts as part of the deal to avoid jail or get their records expunged. The treatment is really an outpatient course in the party line, and the patients are deemed to have recovered if they acknowledge that they were addicts. The more people they arrest and send to treatment the more they will claim that this justifies arresting more people.
See
Calling All Quacks: The Therapeutic Police State and the Politicization of Medicine. Doctors Cannot Study The Violence of Cannabis Prohibition. Because They Are The Disease, Not The Cure.

Drug Czar Decries Ariz. Pot Measure
October 11, 2002
By SANDY YANG, Associated Press Writer

PHOENIX (AP) - The federal drug czar denounced a measure on Arizona's November ballot that would decriminalize possession of small amounts of marijuana, calling it a " stupid, insulting con. "

John P. Walters made the statement Wednesday at a town hall meeting, and on Thursday visited a center for teen drug addicts in Nevada to criticize a similar measure there.

" We know that marijuana is the single largest source of dependency, " Walters, head of the Office of National Drug Control Policy, told a group of about 150 senior citizens and children Wednesday. " We know that it is responsible for 20 percent of accidents on the road today.
(MarijuanaNews note: There is really no data to support that claim.)
See
UK Study on Marijuana and Driving Again Shows That It Is Not A Significant Factor in Accidents. Should We Arrest People for Being Tired?
and links.

" How many billions of dollars in liability is Arizona opening itself up to down the line? "

If passed, Arizona's Proposition 203 would decriminalize the possession of up to two ounces of marijuana for personal use. It would also require the Department of Public Safety to provide free marijuana to people with a written recommendation from a physician.

In Nevada on Thursday, Walters said, " no community is better off with more drugs. " He has said Nevada's Question 9 could make the state a center for drug tourism.

Billy Rogers, head of Nevadans for Responsible Law Enforcement, the main group supporting the measure, said there's no evidence the initiative's passage would create more drug addicts.

He pointed out that the drug czar's own Web site shows the majority of drug addicts in Nevada were treated last year for an amphetamine addiction.

" I think it's about time the drug czar was held accountable to the outright falsehoods he's been putting out there, " Rogers said.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is one of the few news stories that actually cites facts that contradict the Czar. If this continues it will fundamentally change journalism.)
See
Letter to the Editors of the Seattle Times. Someone Is Lying to You. Supporters Of Cannabis Prohibition Need to Do A Credibility Check.

Phoenix resident Carolyn Barker, 60, attended Wednesday's meeting because she was angered at comments that Walters made on the radio earlier in the day.

" I had a friend with cancer and it helped him eat, " Barker said. " He got marijuana illegally and he could have gotten caught. "

Walters, who coordinates federal drug programs and spending, said no scientific data proves marijuana is effective as medicine.

(MarijuanaNews note: Lies have consequences. I received the following from California NORML today. It proves that the real target of cannabis prohibition is the suppression of medical cannabis. This is the reason for the lying, to justify attacks on the sick and dying and those who help them. This also fits my own definition of evil.)

SAN DIEGO, Oct 11: Steve McWilliams of the Shelter from the Storm Cannabis Collective was arrested on federal charges of cultivation today at 8 AM. He is being charged for growing a 20-plant home garden that was raided by the DEA on Sept. 24th. This is the smallest known marijuana case to be criminally prosecuted by the federal government in its crackdown on medical marijuana in California. Steve is expected to be released later today on bail, according to his partner, Barbara MacKenzie.
